What CTET Paper 2 asks on Introduction to Algebra

Questions cover variables, constants, terms and coefficients, forming and simplifying algebraic expressions, and solving simple linear equations, plus translating word statements into expressions.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • A variable is a letter standing for an unknown; a constant is a fixed number.
  • The coefficient is the numerical factor of a term (in 5x it is 5).
  • Only like terms can be added or subtracted: 3x + 5x = 8x, but 3x + 5y cannot be combined.
  • Golden rule of equations: do the same operation to both sides.
  • “5 more than x” is x + 5; “7 less than twice y” is 2y − 7.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Combining unlike terms (adding 3x and 5y).
  • Applying an operation to only one side of an equation.
  • Confusing an expression (no equals sign) with an equation.

questions.q: What is the numerical coefficient of the term -7x²y in the algebraic expression 5x³ - 7x²y + 9xy - 4?
questions.explanation: The numerical coefficient of a term is its constant numerical factor, written without the variables attached to it. In the term -7x²y, that numerical factor is -7.

questions.q: Classify the algebraic expression 3x² - 5xy + 2y² based on the number of terms.
questions.explanation: An expression containing three unlike terms is called a trinomial. Here, the terms are 3x², -5xy, and 2y².

questions.q: What is the sum of 3x² - 5x + 2 and -x² + 2x - 7?
Find the solution of the linear equation: 5x - 3 = 2x + 9.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x - 3 = 9. Add 3 to both sides: 3x = 12. Divide by 3: x = 4.

questions.q: Find the product of the binomials: (2x - 3)(3x + 4).

questions.explanation: Work from the innermost bracket outward. Innermost: (y - 2x). Braces: x - (y - 2x) = x - y + 2x = 3x - y. Brackets: y - (3x - y) = y - 3x + y = 2y - 3x. Finally: 4x - (2y - 3x) = 4x - 2y + 3x = 7x - 2y.

questions.q: The present age of a father is three times the age of his son. After 10 years, the father's age will be twice the age of his son. Find the present age of the son.
questions.explanation: Let son's present age be x years. Father's present age = 3x. After 10 years, son's age = x + 10, father's age = 3x + 10. Given 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10) \implies 3x + 10 = 2x + 20 \implies x = 10.
Rearrange terms with x on one side: x/2 - x/3 = 1/2 + 1/4. The LCM of 2 and 3 is 6, and 1/2+1/4=3/4: 3x - 2x/6 = 3/4 \implies x/6 = 3/4 \implies x = 4.5.

questions.q: Think of a number, multiply it by 5, add 7 to the result, and then divide the sum by 2. If the final result is 26, what was the original number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. Equation: 5x + 7/2 = 26 \implies 5x + 7 = 52 \implies 5x = 45 \implies x = 9.

questions.q: Seema has ₹x. Rohit has ₹15 more than twice of what Seema has. Which expression represents total money both have together?
questions.explanation: Seema's money = x. Rohit's money = 2x + 15. Total money = x + (2x + 15) = 3x + 15.

faq.q: What is the difference between an expression and an equation?
faq.a: An expression (like 2x + 3) has no equals sign; an equation (like 2x + 3 = 11) states that two expressions are equal and can be solved.
